finding.claim: A Buffer-encoded (DER/SPKI) public key with no algorithms restriction (or an algorithms list including HS*) is misclassified as an HMAC secret, so an attacker who knows the public key can forge HS256/384/512 tokens.
finding.source: Verifier key option given as a Buffer containing DER public key bytes (also via key-fetcher return values, verifier.js:456-464); attacker controls token header alg=HS256 and signs with the public key bytes.
finding.sink: verifySignature HS branch createHmac(alg, key) at src/crypto.js:389-391, with key = createSecretKey(DER bytes) at src/verifier.js:524.

trace.note: Non-function key goes to detectPublicKeyAlgorithms(key, allowedAlgorithms)
Buffer converted with toString('utf-8'); DER bytes become replacement characters
locatePem finds no -----BEGIN header, so isRawSecret is true
assertNotAsymmetricJwkJson only detects JSON JWK/JWKS, not DER, so it does not fire
Returns hsAlgorithms as the allowed set
allowedAlgorithms set to HS256/384/512 because none were configured
prepareKeyOrSecret(key, true) produces createSecretKey(DER bytes)
header.alg allowlist passes for HS256 because the list was derived from the key
HMAC over token input with DER bytes as secret; timingSafeEqual matches the attacker's MAC

finding.guards_checked: Algorithm allowlist verifier.js:162 (passes, list derived from key). PEM matchers crypto.js:27-28,40 (anchored on BEGIN, DER never matches). isAsymmetricJwkJson crypto.js:93-115 (JSON only). checkAreCompatibleAlgorithms verifier.js:19-31 (safe when algorithms is RS/ES-only, throws). HMAC catch crypto.js:391-392 (safe for PEM public keys, which become KeyObjects that HMAC rejects). Async path verifier.js:456-464 has the same flaw.

finding.claim: With the verifier cache enabled, a token that has exp but no iat is cached with a TTL of cacheTTL that ignores exp, so an expired token is accepted from cache until that TTL elapses.
finding.source: Token payload with exp and no iat (e.g. signer noTimestamp:true with expiresIn). Attacker replays a previously valid token after expiry.
finding.sink: Cache-hit return at src/verifier.js:377, which skips verifyToken and therefore the exp validator at verifier.js:606-613 and validateClaimDateValue at verifier.js:198-205.

trace.note: First verification at t0 runs exp check and passes while token is valid
hasIat is false, so the exp branch in cacheSet is skipped
cacheValue[2] initialized to 0
cacheValue[2] stays 0, so it becomes maxTTL = now + clockTolerance + cacheTTL, ignoring exp
Later verify: cache lookup by token hash
min === 0 and now <= max both hold after exp
handleCachedResult returns cached payload as valid

finding.guards_checked: iat gate verifier.js:117 (root cause). min(exp, maxTTL) clamp verifier.js:134 caps only at cacheTTL, not exp. Cache is off by default (verifier.js:580, createCache crypto/verifier.js:83-86), so precondition is cache: true or a number.

finding.claim: With complete:true, the async path returns input as the full JWT including signature, while the sync path returns header.payload only, so the two modes disagree on what input means.
finding.sink: Returned decoded object field input; callers that re-verify the signature over input get different bytes depending on sync vs async.

trace.note: Sync path returns input = header.payload (decoder slice)
Async path returns input: token (full JWT)

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification itself uses the correct input (verifier.js:280, 466), so no auth bypass. Impact limited to caller misuse of input.

finding.claim: With cache enabled, passing a Buffer token throws an uncaught TypeError from hashToken instead of a TokenError, bypassing the callback and error handling.
finding.source: Attacker-sent token bytes passed by the app as a Buffer (verifier.js:353 accepts Buffer).
finding.sink: cacheKeyBuilder(token) to hashToken at src/utils.js:45-46 calling token.split on a Buffer, outside any try block.

trace.note: Buffer tokens accepted
cache.get(cacheKeyBuilder(token)) runs outside try
token.split('.', 1) on a Buffer throws TypeError

finding.guards_checked: Fail-closed: the request is rejected, not accepted. Impact is an exception-type mismatch that may produce a 500 or an unhandled error in the caller.
